summary: End of the win_whoami example output (privileges, logon rights, token_type, upn) and how to read label.account_name: Medium means Ansible got a limited token without admin rights, High means an elevated token with all privileges, System means NT AUTHORITY\System.
questions: How do I tell if an Ansible Windows task ran elevated?
What does a Medium mandatory label mean in win_whoami?
Why does my Windows task not have administrative rights?
What does label System mean in win_whoami?

answer_card.title: Check whether a Windows task ran with admin rights
answer_card.answer_md:
Run `ansible.windows.win_whoami` with become and look at `label.account_name`:

- **Medium**: Ansible could not get an elevated token. Only some privileges are available and the user has no admin rights.
- **High**: an elevated token was used and all of the user's privileges are available.
- **System**: the `NT AUTHORITY\System` account was used, the highest level available.
